name: Solitude-Frozen
geological_features: Vast tundra plains supporting cold-adapted vegetation
Frozen mountain ranges with permanent ice waterfalls
Geothermally heated valleys creating oases of relative warmth
specific_features: A single structure of alien origin in the deepest valley, emitting consistent heat
description: Solitude-Frozen is a large ice world that defies the sterile expectations of its type, harboring a breathable atmosphere and cold-adapted flora across its vast tundra plains. Frozen mountain ranges glitter under pale sunlight, their faces streaked with ice waterfalls that have not flowed in millennia, while geothermally heated valleys shelter pockets of denser vegetation in microclimates that approach merely frigid.

The breathable atmosphere tastes of cold metal and pine-analogous resins from the hardy flora that carpets the lower elevations. The world is profoundly still, its distances immense, its horizons empty, a place where one could walk for months without encountering another living thing larger than a frost-adapted shrub.

In the deepest geothermal valley, partially buried in accumulated snow, stands a structure of alien origin that radiates consistent heat from an internal source that has not diminished in the decades since its discovery. The structure's architecture suggests a dwelling rather than a machine, but its single doorway opens onto an interior that instruments cannot map and cameras cannot photograph, returning only static.

The rare flora that grows in the heated zone around the structure produces compounds found nowhere else on the planet, suggesting the heat source has influenced local evolution over a geological timespan. Solitude-Frozen offers livable conditions for those willing to endure the isolation and the cold, but the structure in the valley poses questions that no colonization plan has satisfactorily addressed.
